🚨🇲🇽 <u>DECLASSIFIED: THE CALDERÓN YEARS WERE US INTERVENTION AT ITS PEAK</u>

Newly declassified US Embassy cables detail the deepest American penetration of Mexican security under Felipe Calderón: the Mérida Initiative wired García Luna's "Plataforma México" surveillance grid across 600+ monitoring points and 169 federal police stations, funneled polygraph and gamma-ray inspection tech into CISEN, Sedena and the PGR, and trained Mexican police on US soil — all while the failed Fast & Furious operation walked high-caliber weapons to the Sinaloa Cartel. García Luna, once decorated by the DEA as Mexico's "best" officer, now sits in a US prison for taking that same cartel's money.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>DECLASSIFIED FILES TIE THE PAN TO THE FAR-RIGHT KNIGHTS OF COLUMBUS</u>

Declassified Mexican security files (DFS, "box 16, bundle one") document three decades of ties between the National Action Party (PAN) and the ultra-right Knights of Columbus — a Catholic order with 8,000–10,000 members across 100+ councils by the mid-1960s. Agents placed Knights-linked youth inside PAN electoral brigades as far back as 1962, and former PAN national president José González Torres appears in the files at the order's ceremonies. Their agenda against secular education, reproductive rights and LGBTQ+ rights, Contralínea notes, "continues in the present."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM CALLS INE'S 42-BILLION-PESO BUDGET "EXAGGERATED"</u>

On the eve of the 2027 electoral process, Mexico's electoral authority INE is asking for nearly 42 billion pesos — a request President Sheinbaum called "exaggerated," saying 37 billion (2024 spending plus inflation) is more than enough to run the vote. She also questioned why the INE would suddenly change its institutional color right before the election: "It would be good if the INE president or the councillors clarified all these doubts, so there's no doubt about the 2027 electoral process."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>PAN GOVERNOR OPENS US-LINKED SPY TOWER — MEXICO'S GOVERNMENT STAYS AWAY</u>

PAN governor Maru Campos inaugurated her "Torre Centinela" surveillance complex in Ciudad Juárez — with the US consul general and officials from Las Cruces, New Mexico present, but no one from Sheinbaum's federal government. US consul Katharine Beamer called the tower "important to strengthen security capacities in the region"; at the perimeter, protesters denounced the state's surveillance collaboration with Washington.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>TRUMP'S 25% TARIFFS — AND MEXICO'S AUTO EXPORTS STILL ROSE</u>

In August, Mexico exported 300,475 light vehicles — up 1.26% year-on-year, 3,741 more units than August 2025 — even with Washington's 25% auto tariffs in force since April 2025, per INEGI's RAIAVL registry. Production eased 1.43% to 344,940 units, but the export engine held. The tariffs sold as a way to drag the industry north keep failing to.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>SINALOA MAKES RECRUITING KIDS A CRIME — UP TO 30 YEARS</u>

Sinaloa's Congress unanimously turned the forced recruitment of minors into a standalone crime: 10 to 20 years in prison, up to 30 if the recruiter is a relative, guardian, or public official — and the child is legally a victim of organized crime, not a criminal. The urgency is in one number: minors jailed for serious crimes in the state jumped from 4 in 2024 to 96 by December 2025. The law mandates rescue and reintegration protocols across all three levels of government.

🇲🇽📰 <u>PROTECT THE PRESS — AND FINALLY CLOSE THE CASES</u>

On International Journalists' Day, Mexico's National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) called to "strengthen actions to protect journalists and guarantee the right to inform," while admitting there is still "a debt in the investigation and resolution of cases of violence" — above all at the local level, where organized crime reaches. It credited eight years of advances in press protection and its round-the-clock protection program, but was clear the risk hasn't gone. Impunity, not shortage of words, is the unfinished part.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>THE RIGHT WANTS ONE VOTE PER HOUSEHOLD — NOT PER WOMAN</u>

PAN activist Javier Albarrán has floated "household voting" in Mexico — concentrating a family's ballots in one person to strengthen "the family as society's basic cell." UNAM political scientist Ana Karen Cortés warns of "very important networks and power groups seeking to eliminate the participation of women and historically marginalized groups." Mexican women have only held citizenship for three or four generations; the tradwife-to-household-vote pipeline, imported straight from Turning Point USA, is built to claw that back.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>NO MORE UNTOUCHABLES: SAT TO AUDIT UNIONS AND GOVERNORS</u>

Sheinbaum's 2027 budget bill would put unions and state and municipal governments under the tax authority (SAT) — bodies long exempt from real fiscal scrutiny. The initiative wants the SAT to verify their income "matches its purpose and complies with the tax provisions applicable to them." Until now unions kept no accounting and issued no tax receipts, while local governments only had to withhold and remit — feeding the perception they answered to no one. That perception is what's ending.

⚖️🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S TOP COURT: HOME-COOKED CANNABIS IS A RIGHT</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court ruled 7-2 that an adult with a personal-use permit can cook cannabis into their own food — brownies, edibles, all of it — calling it "an ordinary culinary activity," not pharmaceutical manufacturing subject to special sanitary controls. Justice Lenia Batres's project orders Cofepris to grant the permit; sale, distribution and supply to others stay banned. While Marco Rubio lectures Mexico on drugs, its own courts keep widening personal freedom on Mexican terms.
